# Apparatus for Determining the Relationship Between Surface and Internal Body Motion

## Overview

The present invention provides an apparatus designed to determine the relationship between the surface motion of a body and the internal motion of an object located within that body. By establishing a correlation between externally observable movement and the movement of internal structures, the apparatus enables improved tracking and prediction of internal motion based on more readily accessible surface measurements.

## First Sensing Unit

The apparatus includes a first sensing unit configured to acquire a position signal from a first element. This first element is placed at a location on the body's surface, allowing the sensing unit to track the surface motion of the body over time. As the surface of the body moves, the first sensing unit captures corresponding positional data that reflects this external movement.

## Second Sensing Unit

In addition, the apparatus incorporates a second sensing unit that acquires a position signal from a second element. This second element is attached to an interventional device that is placed on or within the internal object. Through this arrangement, the second sensing unit is able to monitor the motion of the internal object as reflected by the movement of the interventional device.

## Synchronous Signal Acquisition

A key feature of the apparatus is that the first and second position signals are acquired synchronously over a given duration. By capturing both the surface motion and the internal motion simultaneously across the same time period, the apparatus ensures that the two data sets are temporally aligned. This synchronous acquisition enables an accurate and meaningful comparison between the external and internal movements.

## Third Unit for Relationship Calculation

Finally, the apparatus features a third unit that calculates the relationship between the surface motion and the internal object motion. This calculation is based on the two position signals acquired by the first and second sensing units. By analyzing the correlation between the synchronously recorded signals, the third unit is able to determine how the surface motion relates to the corresponding internal motion, thereby providing valuable insight into the dynamic behavior of the internal object.

## Summary

Taken together, the components of this apparatus—the first sensing unit, the second sensing unit, and the third calculation unit—work in concert to establish a reliable relationship between externally observable surface motion and the internal motion of an object within the body. This capability has significant potential for applications requiring precise monitoring and prediction of internal movement based on surface measurements.

# Determining the Relationship Between Body Surface Motion and Internal Object Motion

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to an apparatus and method for determining the relationship between the motion of a body's surface and the motion of an object located within or on that body. More particularly, the invention concerns the correlation of externally observable surface movements with the movement of internal anatomical structures, which is of significant value in the field of image-guided interventional procedures.

## Background

During many medical interventions, physicians must guide instruments toward or into internal structures that are subject to continuous motion. Such motion frequently arises from physiological processes, most notably respiration, but also from cardiac activity and other involuntary movements. Because internal structures may shift substantially in position during these cycles, accurately tracking and targeting them poses a considerable challenge. A method that allows the internal motion of an object to be inferred from readily accessible external surface motion would therefore offer meaningful advantages for both the accuracy and the safety of interventional procedures.

## Summary of the Invention

The invention addresses the problem of determining the relationship between a body's surface motion and the motion of an internal object. To accomplish this, the invention provides an apparatus that synchronously acquires position signals from two distinct sensing elements. A first sensing element is arranged on the surface of the body, where it detects movements of the external surface—such as those produced by respiration. A second sensing element is attached to an interventional device that is positioned on or within the internal object, allowing it to detect the motion of that object directly.

By acquiring the position signals from both sensing elements in a synchronized manner, the apparatus obtains temporally aligned data describing external and internal motion simultaneously. From these synchronized position signals, the invention calculates the relationship between the surface motion and the internal object motion. This calculated relation establishes a correlation between the two, enabling external surface movements to serve as an indicator of the corresponding internal motion.

## Advantages and Applications

Once the relationship between surface motion and internal object motion has been established, it can be used to estimate the position of the internal object based on observations of the external surface alone. This capability is particularly significant for tracking and guiding interventional procedures, as it allows a clinician to anticipate and follow the movement of an internal target without requiring continuous direct observation of that target. As a result, the invention supports more precise navigation of interventional devices, improves the reliability of targeting moving structures, and may contribute to reduced procedural risk and improved clinical outcomes.

counterfactuals.output:
# Abstract

An apparatus and method for measuring and correlating the motion of an external surface of a body with the motion of an internal object disposed within the body. The apparatus comprises one or more position sensors configured to detect and track movement of the external surface, and one or more position sensors configured to detect and track movement of the internal object. A processing unit is operatively coupled to the position sensors and configured to receive positional data from both the external and internal sensors over a period of time. The processing unit determines a spatial and temporal relationship between the external surface motion and the internal object motion by analyzing the correlated positional data. In certain embodiments, the processing unit generates a predictive model that estimates the position of the internal object based on subsequently measured external surface motion, thereby enabling real-time tracking of the internal object without continuous direct measurement thereof. The apparatus may be employed in applications requiring precise localization of an internal target that moves in response to physiological or mechanical motion of the surrounding body, including but not limited to medical imaging, radiation therapy, surgical guidance, and industrial monitoring. The disclosed system provides improved accuracy in predicting internal object displacement, reduces the need for invasive or repeated internal measurements, and facilitates dynamic compensation for motion during procedures.

# Patent Summary

## System for Correlating Body Surface Movement with Internal Object Movement

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to systems and methods for tracking the movement of an internal object within a patient's body by correlating externally measured body surface motion with the motion of an internal object monitored via an interventional device.

### Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a system for correlating body surface movement with the movement of an internal anatomical object or region of interest. The system comprises a first sensing unit, a second sensing unit, and a calculation unit operatively coupled thereto.

**First Sensing Unit:** The first sensing unit is configured to detect and measure movement of a body surface of a patient. In embodiments, the first sensing unit may comprise one or more of an optical sensor, a pressure sensor, a strain gauge, an accelerometer, or a camera-based system arranged to acquire a signal representative of surface displacement over time. The body surface movement may correspond to respiratory motion, cardiac motion, or other physiological cycles that induce periodic or quasi-periodic displacement of the body surface.

**Second Sensing Unit:** The second sensing unit is associated with an interventional device positionable within the patient's body. The second sensing unit is configured to track the position and/or movement of an internal object, such as a target lesion, organ, or anatomical landmark, relative to or by means of the interventional device. In embodiments, the interventional device may comprise a catheter, needle, guidewire, endoscope, or implantable sensor, and the second sensing unit may employ electromagnetic tracking, optical shape sensing, ultrasound, or imaging-based localization to determine the position of the internal object.

**Calculation Unit:** The calculation unit is configured to receive a first signal from the first sensing unit representative of body surface movement and a second signal from the second sensing unit representative of internal object movement. The calculation unit is further configured to establish a correlation, correspondence, or mapping between the body surface movement and the internal object movement. Based upon this correlation, the calculation unit may generate a correlation model that permits estimation of the internal object position from subsequently measured body surface movement.

In operation, the system enables the position of the internal object to be estimated or predicted from surface measurements alone once the correlation model has been established, thereby reducing reliance on continuous internal tracking. The system may thus facilitate applications including, without limitation, image-guided intervention, radiation therapy gating, motion compensation, and real-time procedural guidance.

### Advantages

The disclosed system provides improved accuracy in localizing a moving internal object by leveraging a correlation between readily accessible surface motion and internal motion tracked via an interventional device. This may reduce the need for continuous imaging or invasive monitoring, minimize patient exposure to ionizing radiation, and enhance the precision and safety of interventional and therapeutic procedures.

---

*Note: This is a drafting template. A qualified patent attorney or agent should review and tailor the claims and specification to the specific invention and applicable jurisdictional requirements.*

# Technical Invention Description: Medical Device for Correlating Patient Surface Motion with Internal Target Motion

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a medical device and method for determining the correlation between a patient's external surface motion and the motion of an internal organ or anatomical target. More particularly, the invention pertains to a system that establishes a real-time motion model enabling internal target tracking based on externally observable surface displacement.

## Background

Many medical interventions—including radiotherapy, biopsy, ablation, and minimally invasive surgery—require precise targeting of internal organs. However, internal targets such as the lungs, liver, and kidneys move continuously due to respiration, cardiac activity, and voluntary patient movement. Direct continuous imaging of internal motion (e.g., via fluoroscopy) exposes the patient to cumulative radiation and is often impractical during an intervention. There exists a need for a system that infers internal target motion from a non-invasive surrogate signal.

## Summary of the Invention

The invention comprises three principal components:

1. A **first sensing unit** configured to acquire surface motion data from the patient's body.
2. A **second sensing unit** attached to an interventional device, configured to acquire positional data associated with an internal target region.
3. A **calculating unit** configured to compute a correlation model relating the surface motion to the internal target motion.

---

## Detailed Description

### 1. First Sensing Unit (Surface Motion Detection)

The first sensing unit is arranged externally relative to the patient and is configured to detect motion of the patient's body surface, for example the anterior thorax or abdominal wall.

**Embodiments may include:**
- An optical sensor arrangement (e.g., a structured-light or time-of-flight camera) that captures displacement of the skin surface without physical contact.
- One or more fiducial markers or reflective elements placed on the patient's skin, tracked by an optical tracking subsystem.
- A pressure- or strain-based belt sensor providing a respiratory surrogate signal.
- An inertial measurement unit (IMU) affixed to the surface.

The first sensing unit outputs a **surface motion signal** \( S_{ext}(t) \), representing one or more degrees of freedom (e.g., anterior–posterior displacement) as a function of time.

### 2. Second Sensing Unit (Internal Target Reference)

The second sensing unit is mechanically attached to, or integrated within, an **interventional device**. The interventional device may be a needle, catheter, endoscope, ablation probe, or guidewire that is introduced into or positioned near the internal organ or target.

**The second sensing unit may comprise:**
- An electromagnetic (EM) tracking sensor whose position and orientation are determined within a generated field.
- A fiber-optic shape-sensing element (e.g., fiber Bragg grating).
- An ultrasound transducer or transponder providing localized positional data.
- A radiopaque marker tracked by intermittent imaging.

Because the interventional device is placed at or in known geometric relation to the internal target, the second sensing unit provides an **internal motion signal** \( P_{int}(t) \) representative of the actual displacement of the internal organ or target.

### 3. Calculating Unit (Correlation Model)

The calculating unit is communicatively coupled to both sensing units and receives the surface motion signal \( S_{ext}(t) \) and the internal motion signal \( P_{int}(t) \).

**The calculating unit is configured to:**

**(a) Temporal synchronization** — time-align the two signals to a common clock, compensating for any acquisition latency.

**(b) Correlation model derivation** — compute a mathematical relationship \( f \) such that:

$$ P_{int}(t) \approx f\big(S_{ext}(t)\big) $$

This model may be:
- A **linear regression** or affine mapping between surface and internal displacement;
- A **polynomial or higher-order model** accounting for hysteresis between inhalation and exhalation phases;
- A **machine-learning model** (e.g., a neural network or state-space filter) trained on a paired data set collected during a calibration phase.

**(c) Predictive estimation** — once the correlation model is established, the calculating unit estimates the internal target position **from the surface signal alone**, allowing the interventional device or a therapy delivery system to be guided or gated without continuous internal imaging.

**(d) Model validation and updating** — the calculating unit may periodically compare predicted internal positions against intermittent measurements from the second sensing unit, updating the correlation model to account for drift or physiological changes.

---

## Operation

1. **Calibration phase:** Both sensing units acquire data simultaneously over one or more physiological cycles. The calculating unit derives the correlation model.
2. **Guidance/monitoring phase:** The internal target position is continuously predicted from the surface signal. Optionally, the second sensing unit provides periodic verification.
3. **Output:** The estimated internal target position is provided to a display, a gating controller (e.g., for beam-on/beam-off in radiotherapy), or a robotic guidance system.

---

## Advantages

- Reduces reliance on continuous internal imaging and associated radiation exposure.
- Provides real-time, patient-specific correlation between surface and internal motion.
- Accounts for non-linear and hysteretic relationships between external and internal movement.
- Enables adaptive updating during a procedure to maintain targeting accuracy.

---

## Claims (Illustrative)

**Claim 1.** A medical device comprising: a first sensing unit configured to acquire a surface motion signal representative of motion of a patient's body surface; a second sensing unit attached to an interventional device and configured to acquire an internal motion signal representative of motion of an internal organ or target; and a calculating unit configured to determine a correlation between the surface motion signal and the internal motion signal, and to estimate a position of the internal organ or target based on said correlation.

**Claim 2.** The device of Claim 1, wherein the calculating unit is further configured to predict the position of the internal organ or target from the surface motion signal after the correlation is established.

**Claim 3.** The device of Claim 1, wherein the correlation accounts for hysteresis between an inhalation phase and an exhalation phase.

**Claim 4.** The device of Claim 1, wherein the second sensing unit comprises one of an electromagnetic tracking sensor, a fiber-optic shape sensor, or an ultrasound-based positional sensor.

**Claim 5.** The device of Claim 1, wherein the calculating unit periodically updates the correlation using verification measurements from the second sensing unit.

---

*Note: This description is a technical drafting aid. For an actual patent filing, consult a registered patent attorney or agent to ensure novelty, adequate prior-art searching, and jurisdiction-specific claim formatting.*

# Summary of the Invention

## Overview

The present invention provides an apparatus and method for determining a motion relation between a body surface and an internal object of a subject. In accordance with embodiments of the invention, position signals representative of the motion of a body surface and position signals representative of the motion of an internal object are acquired synchronously, and a correlation relationship between the two is established. This relationship enables the position of the internal object to be estimated from measurements of the body surface motion during subsequent operations, thereby facilitating applications such as image-guided intervention, radiation therapy, and diagnostic imaging.

## Summary

In one aspect, the invention provides an apparatus comprising:

- a first sensing arrangement configured to acquire a first position signal representative of a motion of a body surface of a subject;
- a second sensing arrangement configured to acquire a second position signal representative of a motion of an internal object of the subject;
- a synchronization unit configured to temporally align the first position signal and the second position signal such that the acquired signals correspond to substantially the same instants in time; and
- a processor configured to determine, from the synchronously acquired first and second position signals, a motion relation that relates the motion of the body surface to the motion of the internal object.

In some embodiments, the first sensing arrangement comprises one or more of an optical marker system, an optical surface-imaging system, a range-imaging camera, a strain gauge, a pressure belt, or another external surface-tracking device. The second sensing arrangement may comprise an imaging modality such as an ultrasound system, a fluoroscopic imaging system, a magnetic resonance imaging system, a computed tomography system, or an implanted or transponder-based localization device configured to track the internal object.

In a further aspect, the processor is configured to derive the motion relation by computing a correlation model, which may include a linear model, a polynomial model, a piecewise model, or a model incorporating temporal derivatives to account for phase differences and hysteresis between the body surface motion and the internal object motion. In certain embodiments, the motion relation is represented as a model that predicts a position, displacement, or trajectory of the internal object as a function of a measured position of the body surface.

In another aspect, the processor is further configured to update the motion relation over time using subsequently acquired position signals, thereby accommodating changes in the motion relation arising from physiological variations, drift, or changes in respiratory or cardiac patterns.

In a further aspect, once the motion relation has been determined, the apparatus is configured to estimate a position of the internal object based on a subsequently acquired first position signal representative of the body surface motion, without requiring continuous direct measurement of the internal object. This enables, for example, the gating or tracking of a therapeutic or diagnostic device relative to the estimated position of the internal object.

## Method Summary

In accordance with a further aspect, the invention provides a method comprising:

- acquiring a first position signal representative of a motion of a body surface of a subject;
- synchronously acquiring a second position signal representative of a motion of an internal object of the subject;
- temporally aligning the first and second position signals; and
- determining, from the aligned first and second position signals, a motion relation that relates the motion of the body surface to the motion of the internal object.

In some embodiments, the method further comprises estimating a position of the internal object from a subsequently acquired first position signal using the determined motion relation, and optionally controlling a device, such as a radiation delivery system or an imaging system, in dependence on the estimated position.

## Advantages

Embodiments of the invention provide one or more of the following advantages. By synchronously acquiring the position signals, the invention establishes an accurate temporal correspondence between the external and internal motions, improving the reliability of the derived motion relation. The invention allows the position of an internal object to be estimated from readily measurable external surface motion, reducing the need for continuous invasive or radiation-intensive internal imaging. The ability to update the motion relation over time further enhances accuracy in the presence of physiological variability. These and other features and advantages will become apparent from the following detailed description, considered together with the accompanying drawings.

---

*Note: This is a template drafted for illustrative purposes. The claims and specification should be reviewed and tailored by a qualified patent professional to reflect the specific technical details, novelty, and scope of your particular invention.*
